newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM says sees 1997 GDP growth over 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM says sees 1997 GDP growth over 4 pct.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Tuesday that he expected 1997 gross domestic product growth of more than four percent, but that full-year 1996 GDP growth was one percentage point under original expectations.
"I want to say that for this year we foresee economic growth of higher than four percent, which in a European context is a very fitting result," Klaus told the Zofin Forum of Czech business leaders.

He said that industrial output had showed a marked slowing since last November which could not be attributed to seasonal factors, and that "1996 ended with a pace of growth slower than we expected by one percent". He did not say on which forecast the slowing was originally based.

Full-year 1996 figures have yet to be released. In September Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik forecast full-year growth at 4.8 percent, the same as the original forecast on which the 1996 state budget was based.
Klaus said the combination led to a revision in his forecast 1997 growth which was originally 5.4 percent and on which the state budget for the year was based.
